title: Event Coreference Resolution for Contentious Politics Events
abstract: Creates and analyzes a multilingual, multi-source event-coreference dataset for contentious-politics events and measures the contribution of event-coreference resolution to event information collection. The study highlights how separate documents can provide erroneous or partial information about events unless mentions of the same underlying event are resolved together.

admission.reason: The paper is genuinely about multi-source event coreference, but the abstract mainly establishes a new contentious-politics dataset and the utility of coreference for information collection. It does not, from the abstract, add sufficiently specific evidence about workplace continuity, partial identity, abstention, correction, or evidence-combination rules beyond the stronger F1 candidates already available this round.

title: A Latent Dirichlet Model for Unsupervised Entity Resolution
abstract: Presents a probabilistic unsupervised model for resolving records into latent entities. The formulation combines multiple observed attributes rather than relying on a single similarity signal and treats identity assignments as uncertain latent structure.
venue: SIAM International Conference on Data Mining

admission.reason: The probabilistic latent-entity formulation is relevant to F5, but the abstract supplies generic unsupervised entity-resolution evidence rather than incremental correction, explicit reject semantics, enterprise communication evidence, or a new answer to the remaining gaps. Additional generic record-linkage transfer evidence is not enough to justify a reading slot here. The identifier is also UNCHECKED.

title: Online Collective Entity Resolution
abstract: Extends collective entity resolution to an online setting where resolution is performed as new queries or records arrive. It exploits relational evidence while avoiding full recomputation, making it relevant to incremental identity assignment in a growing stream.

admission.reason: Online entity resolution and relational evidence are relevant vocabulary and capabilities, but the open-gap statement already recognizes that incremental entity-resolution literature can revise identity assignments. The abstract does not show a contribution specific to msgloom's remaining stable-ID/history semantics, workplace evidence, or CONTINUE/NEW/UNCERTAIN policy. With an UNCHECKED identity, it does not displace stronger candidates.

title: A Method for Calibrating False-Match Rates in Record Linkage
abstract: Addresses how to choose a record-linkage cutoff after records have been assigned agreement weights. It models observed weights as a mixture of true-match and false-match distributions and estimates the false-match rate associated with alternative thresholds, explicitly supporting controlled identity decisions.
venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

admission.reason: The paper offers useful generic calibration of false-match rates for record-linkage thresholds, but gap-2 is explicitly application-specific: msgloom's relative false-merge/false-split costs and CONTINUE/NEW/UNCERTAIN semantics must be determined from project requirements and empirical evaluation. This paper cannot establish those target-domain costs, and stronger uncertainty-under-shift evidence is available this round. The identifier is UNCHECKED.

title: Cross-Document Event Coreference: Annotations, Experiments, and Observations
abstract: Presents early work on identifying mentions of the same event across different documents, including cross-document event-coreference annotations and experiments. It is a foundational study of event identity across document boundaries rather than ordinary within-document reference resolution.

admission.reason: This is foundational cross-document event-coreference work, but the abstract as summarized does not expose a capability or evidence distinction that materially advances the current gaps beyond the denser and more explicit modern identity/evidence candidates in this round. Historical priority alone is not a reason to consume a reading slot. The identity is UNCHECKED.

title: Relational clustering for multi-type entity resolution
abstract: Studies entity resolution when records are connected by heterogeneous relations. The method combines attribute similarity with relational evidence and performs collective clustering, illustrating how links among surrounding objects can contribute evidence for or against an identity decision.

admission.reason: Combining attributes with relational evidence is relevant to F5, but the abstract remains generic entity-resolution transfer evidence and does not address the current high-value gaps in workplace communication, partial event identity, abstention under drift, or stable correction semantics. The contribution is therefore too indirect for this constrained reading round. The identifier is UNCHECKED.

title: A Hierarchical Distance-dependent Bayesian Model for Event Coreference Resolution
abstract: Introduces a hierarchical distance-dependent Bayesian model for event coreference that jointly captures mention-level and cluster-level information. The model performs event clustering without fixing the number of event identities in advance and uses dependencies among mentions to improve identity decisions.
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics

admission.reason: The hierarchical Bayesian formulation and unfixed number of event clusters are relevant to F1 and clustering, but the abstract does not establish online arrival semantics, explicit abstention, later merge/split correction, workplace evidence, or another unresolved gap strongly enough to justify a slot over the more targeted candidates admitted this round.

title: Controlling false match rates in record linkage using extreme value theory
abstract: Develops a record-linkage thresholding method aimed specifically at controlling false matches. Extreme-value modeling is used to estimate an appropriate decision threshold without requiring a labeled training set, providing transferable evidence for conservative identity assignment and false-link control.

admission.reason: Controlling false matches is relevant to conservative identity assignment, but this is another generic record-linkage threshold method. It does not determine msgloom's application-specific false-merge costs or CONTINUE/NEW/UNCERTAIN semantics and does not address workplace concept drift. It therefore does not materially close an open gap. The identifier is UNCHECKED.

title: Convergence Diagnostics for Entity Resolution
abstract: Reviews Bayesian entity-resolution models that infer partitions of records while quantifying uncertainty and focuses on whether posterior computation has actually converged. The paper is relevant to identity-state reliability because it emphasizes uncertainty in partitions and warns that apparently stable identity assignments may reflect poor inference rather than evidence.
venue: Annual Review of Statistics and Its Application

admission.reason: The paper focuses on convergence diagnostics for Bayesian entity-resolution computation. That can improve inference reliability, but it does not materially strengthen the core capability under review: deciding continuity, rejecting uncertain links, constructing work-matter identity, or correcting identity relationships. Its main claim is therefore outside the highest-value scope. The identifier is UNCHECKED.

title: Fast Bayesian Record Linkage With Record-Specific Disagreement Parameters
abstract: Develops probabilistic record linkage with record-specific disagreement probabilities, improving decisions when common attribute values make identities ambiguous. The method is evaluated against expert-labeled matches and also provides ways to estimate true-positive rate and positive predictive value when full ground truth is unavailable.

admission.reason: Record-specific disagreement probabilities and expert-labeled evaluation are useful F5 techniques, but the abstract does not address incremental identity revision, workplace communication evidence, abstention under stream drift, or partial event identity. It is additional generic linkage evidence rather than a material answer to an open gap.

title: Cross-Document, Cross-Language Event Coreference Annotation Using Event Hoppers
abstract: Develops cross-document and cross-language event-coreference annotation using event hoppers. The annotation framework deliberately supports an inclusive conception of coreference and discusses the evidence annotators use when deciding whether event mentions across documents and languages belong to the same event hopper.

admission.reason: The abstract indicates an intentionally inclusive cross-document event-hopper annotation scheme, but the summary is not sufficient to determine whether that inclusiveness explicitly distinguishes full identity from partial, subevent, membership, or evolving-event relations, or merely broadens ordinary coreference annotation. Admit to F6 only if the paper's annotation guidelines define non-equivalence event relations relevant to gap-5; otherwise it is redundant F1 annotation work. The identity is UNCHECKED.

title: New Insights into Cross-Document Event Coreference: Systematic Comparison and a Simplified Approach
abstract: Systematically compares approaches to cross-document event coreference and analyzes which modeling choices materially affect performance. It proposes a simplified approach while retaining the task's explicit target of clustering mentions that denote the same real-world event.

admission.reason: A systematic comparison of cross-document event-coreference approaches is useful background, but the abstract as summarized does not introduce a new identity relation, workplace evidence source, abstention mechanism, correction model, or global evidence capability that materially closes the current gaps. Method-comparison value alone is insufficient for admission in this targeted round. The identity is UNCHECKED.
